The SDS cause of keeping a federal B and H within Yugoslavia was all but lost." [Interpretation] Could we now based on these theories say that it is your position that the SDS was at that time actively undermining the political and social order of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, I -- I just want to comment on the passages that you've mentioned. I haven't had opportunity to study them. I just -- some of what's appeared on the screen I don't think is accurate, but -- well, yes, the political structure I don't think dealt with social issues, but that the -- yes. I mean, I agree with what -- what's stated in the reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it follow from your report that the SDS took organisational steps in 1991 and 1992 with the view to take control over territories that belong to an internationally recognised state, namely the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, in 1991 there was no internationally recognised state of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but -- and just confining ourselves to that time-frame, 1991, 1992, and the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does it follow from that conclusion that the activities of the SDA and the HDZ, leading to the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, were constitutional and lawful?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: No, I don't think that follows from anything I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it the case based on what you know and what you studied that these were lawful and constitutional activities?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, I'm not a lawyer, so I really can't comment on that. I could comment on the politics of it, if you'd like me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, what were the politics of it, taking into account the fact that these were three constituent peoples?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: I would say that the SDA and the HDZ on these two occasions were engaging in a bit of sharp parliamentary practice, certainly. I think that's all I can say. I would -- in that connection, I would point out that the -- the SDS had -- requested that the issue of Bosnian sovereignty - this is in February 1992 - be referred to the Council for National Affairs. I forget the exact name of a council that was provided for it in the amendments to the Bosnian constitution in 1990, a council that would consider matters that directly impacted the vital interests of one or other of the peoples of -- of BH. It had been agreed at that time in the Assembly that that should be done, and it never was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I cannot really agree, because in assessing Serbian conduct, you put forward political but also legal judgements as to how we were undermining a certain political order, and I'm asking you, did it all happen in a vacuum? Was it not that the other sides were also taking illegal and unconstitutional steps at the same time and provoked a Serbian response? To put it more simply, didn't you comment in your report on the constitution and the legislative arrangements?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: I guess, yes, I did report on constitution and legislative arrangements in -- in my capacity as a expert on the history and politics of the former Yugoslavia and not as a lawyer or a legal scholar. But, yes -- I mean, by all means, I hope it's been made clear in these reports that these -- these events were not taking place in a vacuum, that the steps that the Bosnian Serb leadership, the SDS, was taking were intimately connected with developments in Yugoslavia as a whole and in Bosnia in particular, in particular the obvious drive for independence by the SDA and the HDZ. That's the context that I strived to put them in. As far as any illegal or legal activities by members of those parties, I don't get into that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Should we then reckon that all the legal references to the conduct of the Serbian leadership should also be ignored? Should we ignore all the legal opinions you give about the conduct of Radovan Karadzic and the Serbian leadership?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, that's a bit broad. I'm not quite sure what Dr. Karadzic intends to convey by -- what was it, "legal references." It seems pretty capacious and is certainly vulnerable to misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Karadzic. The difficulty with that is that it opens, again, it really opens a debating shop rather than a cross-examination. There is nothing to stop you making a submission in due course in terms of testimony, anybody's testimony, that certain aspects of it should not be taken into account and give justifications for that. I don't think that we're going to be assisted by going down this particular route with this particular witness. Again, it's entirely a matter for you, but I would have thought you might have been better placed using your time where you have an issue with a conclusion that Dr. Treanor has drawn, challenging or expanding upon that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then I will conclude with this segment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was then the referendum on the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina legal? With regards to Bosnian Serbs, you dealt with legality of regionalisation and all the other actions that were closely connected to the conduct of the two other sides, but what about the referendum on independence on Bosnia-Herzegovina? Was it lawful, was the decision to hold it legal, and was it implemented in a lawful way?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, again I really can't comment on the legality of it, and the technical sense, as I said before, the resolution was -- before it was passed at a rather contentious session of the Bosnian Assembly and could be considered rather sharp practice, but I would comment that the position of the SDS, although they certainly did not favour that because they knew what was going to happen. Then the referendum was held basically at the suggestion of the -- of the so-called Badinter Commission, that that might be an indicator that the results of such a referendum might an indicator that would facilitate other states in making a decision on recognising the independence of Bosnia, that the position of the SDS was, well, we had our plebiscite in November, so now let them have theirs. They can have this referendum, their plebiscite, but we're not going to take part in it. Indeed, there was some discussion of the fact that at the time of the Serbian plebiscite the officials from the other parties didn't really seek to thwart that and it was said that, well, in February, you know, we will let them have their referendum, but it will be results for them, not for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Defence, however, has to deal with your conclusions, and in order to see if those conclusions are correct and accurate, we have to see which path led you to those conclusions. That's why I'm asking you whether to the best of your knowledge the referendum was held as Badinter suggested. Did they get to a two-third majority, and was it ratified by the parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina with a two-third majority vote? And if you could answer briefly, please. Was that referendum held in a lawful way, even taking into account Badinter's recommendations? If you don't know, it's not a problem. Just say so.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, I'll have to say I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: That draws today's proceedings to a close, Dr. Karadzic, and we will adjourn for the day and reassemble at 9.00 a.m. tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of June, 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
